newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin tells Russian agency he in fighting mood.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin tells Russian agency he in fighting mood.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, in his first interview since a heart operation two weeks ago, told RIA news agency on Wednesday that he was in fighting mood and would return to work after a spell in a sanatorium.

"I am in fighting mood. I will probably stay in Barvikha (sanatorium) for some time and then back to work," Yeltsin said. RIA said the interview was filmed while Yeltsin and members of his family were walking in the grounds of the Central Clinical Hospital.

Yeltsin thanked the team of surgeons who had conducted the quintuple bypass surgery on November 5 and said that his heart pains had abated. "I do not feel my heart, it is quite different to before the operation."

Earlier on Wednesday doctors removed Yeltsin's post-operation stitches. Top Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Itar-Tass news agency Yeltsin would leave hospital and move to his Barvikha residence outside Moscow on Thursday afternoon or on Friday.
The 65-year-old Kremlin leader held his first full working meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday.

In his interview with RIA, due to be shown on television later on Wednesday, Yeltsin said he was going to demand an account from every top official of his actions during the president's absence from the Kremlin.
